items.q: How do multi-location dermatology websites rank in Google for each city?
items.a: Every location gets its own indexed URL (e.g. /locations/austin-tx), with unique H1, city-specific service copy, a dedicated LocalBusiness + MedicalClinic schema block, embedded Google Map, NAP consistency, and location-linked reviews. Local pack rankings compound per city, not per brand.

items.q: Can patients book at a specific location without confusion?
items.a: Yes. The booking flow always resolves a location first — either from the URL the patient landed on, a ZIP-code detector, or a location switcher in the header. The patient never has to guess which office they're scheduling with.

items.q: How do you keep 10+ location pages from feeling like copy-paste?
items.a: Shared brand system, unique per-location content: real photography, provider bios pinned to that office, city-specific FAQs, insurance accepted at THAT clinic, driving directions from nearby landmarks, and location-specific reviews. Google reads them as distinct entities — patients feel a local practice, not a chain.

items.q: What if we add or close a location later?
items.a: New locations spin up from a governed template in under a week — same design system, unique content. Closed locations 301 to the nearest sibling with a preserved provider redirect map, so rankings and referrals transfer instead of disappearing.

items.q: Do you handle Google Business Profile setup per location?
items.a: Yes. We claim, verify, and optimize a GBP for each location, wire per-location review capture into the site, and align NAP citations across the top 40 medical directories. Local pack visibility is part of the launch, not an upsell.

items.q: How long does a multi-location dermatology website take to launch?
items.a: 5–7 weeks for 2–4 locations, 7–10 weeks for 5–10 locations, 10–14 weeks for 10+ locations or complex EHR integration. Fixed weekly milestones and a hard launch date at kickoff.
